% glossaries with hyperref and makeindex: a main glossary in the list
% style, acronyms in the long-short style, symbols in the super style, and
% a glossary of notation from \newglossary* in the index style. Terms used
% with \gls, \glspl, \Gls, and \Glspl, in italic, sans-serif, and
% typewriter text, in a footnote, in a theorem, and in a heading. A name
% with makeindex's special characters and no sort key, one with an accent
% and a sort key, and one never used, which is not printed. Each \gls links
% to its entry.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsthm}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\usepackage[acronym,symbols]{glossaries}
\newglossary*{notation}{Notation}
\makeglossaries
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\newglossaryentry{group}{name={group},
  description={a set with an associative operation, an identity, and inverses}}
\newglossaryentry{ring}{name={ring},
  description={an abelian group with a second, distributive operation}}
\newglossaryentry{field}{name={field},
  description={a ring whose nonzero elements form a group}}
\newglossaryentry{etale}{name={\'etale},sort={etale},
  description={flat and unramified}}
\newglossaryentry{marks}{name={bang!at@bar|quote"},
  description={a name with makeindex's special characters}}
\newglossaryentry{pi}{type=symbols,name={\ensuremath{\pi}},sort={pi},
  description={the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter}}
\newglossaryentry{hom}{type=notation,name={Hom},
  description={the set of homomorphisms}}
\newglossaryentry{unused}{name={unused},
  description={an entry no \gls uses}}
\setacronymstyle{long-short}
\newacronym{gcd}{GCD}{greatest common divisor}
\newacronym{lcm}{LCM}{least common multiple}
\begin{document}
\section{Groups}
A \gls{group} has inverses. \Gls{group} theory studies \glspl{group}.
Every \emph{\gls{field}} is a \textsf{\gls{ring}}, and \Glspl{ring} are
\texttt{\glspl{ring}} too.\footnote{A \gls{gcd} need not exist in a
\gls{ring}.}
\section{Computing the \gls{lcm}}
The \gls{gcd} of two numbers divides their \gls{lcm}; a \gls{gcd} again.
\begin{theorem}
An \gls{etale} morphism of \glspl{field} is \gls{marks}.
\end{theorem}
The number \gls{pi} is not in \gls{hom}.
\printglossary[style=list]
\printglossary[type=\acronymtype,style=long]
\printglossary[type=symbols,style=super]
\printglossary[type=notation,style=index]
\end{document}
